caption:
He held proof of who betrayed him. He burned it unread.

In 175 AD the general Avidius Cassius tried to take Rome. When the revolt failed, his letters reached Marcus Aurelius. Marcus burned them without reading a line.

That is stoic leadership: power you hold back still speaks. Marcus Aurelius knew grudges cost the one who keeps them.

Save this for the next time someone crosses you at work.

beats.headline: HE BURNED THE EVIDENCE
beats.voice: He held the names of every traitor in Rome. And he burned them.

beats.headline: A general takes the throne
beats.voice: Syria. A false rumour says the emperor is dead. His best general, Avidius Cassius, declares himself emperor.

beats.headline: But Marcus was alive
beats.voice: But Marcus Aurelius was alive. Within months, Cassius was dead, killed by his own officers.

beats.headline: A chest of letters arrives
beats.voice: Then a chest arrives. The rebel's letters. Inside, every senator who backed him.

beats.headline: He never opened them
beats.voice: Any emperor would read them and start the purge. Marcus burned them without reading a line.
